ai.title: Improve CLI tester efficiency via session continuity and capture
ai.summary: Refined `codebuff-local-cli` agent prompts to enforce single-session continuity and high-value tmux captures, preventing silent session restarts and viewport thrashing. Added `cliSpecificDocs` guidance in `.agents/codebuff-local-cli.ts` and operating heuristics in `.agents/lib/cli-agent-prompts.ts` to prioritize meaningful UI state changes over frequent overlapping captures. New session artifacts in `.agents/sessions/03-06-0850-cli-tester-efficiency/` document baseline vs. post-change metrics, showing a reduction from 21 to 10 tool calls in implementation scenarios. Agents must now explicitly report session failure rather than spawning replacements.

eli5.text: The assistant that tests the chat tool now stays in one continuous session instead of accidentally starting over, and it only captures screenshots of the screen when something important actually changes. As a result, each test takes fewer steps to run, cutting the typical number of actions in half. This is live for internal testers today.

ai.title: Expanded prompt cache debug logging with provider request capture
ai.summary: Added `onCacheDebugProviderRequestBuilt` and `cacheDebugCorrelation` to LLM contracts and agent runtime to capture raw/normalized provider requests during cache debug snapshots. Implemented `createCacheDebugSnapshot` and `enrichCacheDebugSnapshotWithProviderRequest` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/cache-debug.ts` replacing simple file writes with structured JSON snapshots including system/tool hashes and data URL summaries. Shared serialization helpers moved to `common/src/util/cache-debug.ts`. Covers Agent Runtime, SDK, and Common types.

eli5.text: If you ever need to see exactly what prompts the system is sending to the AI models, the logging got a lot more detailed. When developers turn on cache debugging, the system now saves a complete snapshot of the request, including the raw data sent to the provider, a cleaner version of that same data, and summaries of any images or files attached. This makes it much easier to understand why certain responses are being cached or not, since you can inspect the full picture of what was sent in each interaction. The new debugging output is available today wherever prompt caching is used, and it applies to anyone building or testing features that rely on cached AI responses.

ai.title: Swap codex agents for gpt-5.4
ai.summary: Renamed thinker-codex to thinker-gpt and code-reviewer-codex to code-reviewer-gpt, switching underlying model from openai/gpt-5.3-codex to openai/gpt-5.4. Updated base-deep.ts prompts to reference new agent IDs in spec, plan, and review phases. Covers agents/base2, agents/thinker, and agents/reviewer directories.

eli5.text: The assistant has been switched to a newer model for thinking through hard problems and reviewing code. The previous model name was dropped from the instructions; the assistant now tells itself to use the new model when it needs to reason carefully. If you watched the assistant's internal plan, you'd see it call on a different specialist agent for complex steps. This is live today for the assistant's own decision-making, not something you toggle yourself.

ai.title: High reasoning effort for base-deep GPT orchestrator
ai.summary: Added `reasoningOptions: { effort: 'high' }` to the `createBaseDeep` factory in `agents/base2/base-deep.ts`. This configures the `openai/gpt-5.4` model to use high reasoning effort for the Buffy orchestrator agent.

eli5.text: The Buffy orchestrator agent now spends more time thinking through its responses carefully before acting, instead of rushing to give quick answers during complex coding tasks. You'll notice it takes a bit longer to respond in situations where it needs to plan and coordinate multiple steps, but its decisions should be more thoughtful and reliable. This higher-reasoning mode applies specifically to the main orchestrator agent that manages planning, editing, and review workflows.
